contribute.heading: Contribute a problem

start.intro: You get a problem file to add to the content repo through a pull request. Nothing is saved on this site.
start.fromLinkHint: CSES, AtCoder and Kattis links come back with the statement, title, constraints and difficulty filled in. Codeforces and SPOJ block automatic fetching, so those open the form with only the id, judge and link.
start.manualHint: An empty form; you fill in everything, including the statement.
start.edit: Edit a problem in the bank

contribute.intro: Fill in the form and the file updates as you type, checked the same way the content repo’s CI checks it. Then copy or download it into the content repo and open a pull request, or use “Open on GitHub”. Nothing is saved on this site.
contribute.guide: How to write a good problem

notices.fetched: Imported from {judge}: the statement, title, constraints and difficulty (where the judge gives one) are filled in. Check them, then add the answers and explanations.
notices.blockedBefore: {judge} blocks automatic fetching, so only the id, judge and link are filled in. Paste the statement yourself, or use
notices.blockedAfter: once the file is in the repo.
notices.failed: Couldn’t read the problem from {judge} right now, so only the id, judge and link are filled in.
notices.notFound: There’s no problem with the id “{id}”. Starting a new one instead.
notices.editingNote: Ids are permanent: changing it makes a new problem.
notices.invalidLink: That isn’t a problem link from CSES, AtCoder, Kattis, Codeforces or SPOJ.
notices.existing: {id} is already in the bank, so here it is to edit.

fields.title: Original title
fields.titleHint: hidden from players until they finish the problem
fields.author: Your GitHub username
fields.statementHint: copied exactly from the judge, without the title, samples or limits. Keep its LaTeX ($N$, \leq).
fields.constraintsHint: the main clue, so be exact
fields.verified: I checked these limits on the judge page
fields.answersHint: Exactly one intended subject and one intended technique inside it. Other correct approaches are accepted; ones that work but are heavier are overkill.
fields.appearsInHint: (distractors: a greedy problem that should appear in DP sessions)
fields.distractorsHint: techniques someone would plausibly but wrongly pick; any subject
fields.explanationHint: why the intended technique fits; point at the constraint that gives it away
fields.explanationEsHint: optional; players with the UI in Spanish see it
fields.trapsHint: common bugs or wrong ideas; the Spanish version is optional
fields.layersHint: DP problems get a state layer and a transition layer. Other kinds are optional.
fields.deprecated: Retired (deprecated). Never delete a problem file; retire it instead.
fields.subject: Subject

layer.optionsHint: Options are a, b, c… in this order. Tick the correct ones. The Spanish “why” is optional.

preview.heading: The file
preview.noPath: The path appears once there’s an id and an intended subject.
preview.notStarted: Start with the id, title and summary; problems CI would reject show up here.
preview.ok: Looks good: this passes the same checks as the content repo’s CI.
preview.statement: The statement as players see it
